主要内容: On July 18, 2012, the Financial Stability Oversight Council (FSOC) designated eight financial market utilities (FMUs) as systemically important under Title VIII of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act. These FMUs include entities such as The Clearing House Payments Company, L.L.C., CLS Bank International, Chicago Mercantile Exchange, Inc., and The Depository Trust Company. The designation subjects these firms to heightened risk management standards. The FSOC considered four factors when determining systemic importance: the aggregate monetary value of transactions processed, exposure to counterparties, interdependencies with other FMUs, and the effect of failure on critical markets. The Council’s decision followed a process that included notifying FMUs of proposed designations and allowing them 30 days to request a hearing, which none did. This action marks a key step in creating a safer financial system under Wall Street Reform. The Council also approved its 2012 Annual Report, which outlines its activities and findings on financial market issues.

股票实体.名称: The Clearing House Payments Company, L.L.C.
